title.en: Unified Legislation Regulatory Ontology: Education Funding Regulations Across Four Jurisdictions (United Kingdom, United States, Canada, Australia)

description.en:
A unified regulatory ontology covering education funding regulations from four jurisdictions (UK, US, Canada, Australia), layered over the Core Compliance Ontology (CCO). Contains 1,295 named classes with 362 cross-jurisdiction 
SKOS alignments.

bibliographicCitation.value: Arshad, U., Corsar, D., Nkisi-Orji, I. (2026). Synthesising Regulatory Ontologies: A Schema and Pattern-Guided Approach

abstract.value: Ontology engineering is a complex, time-consuming, and error-prone process, and is particularly demanding in regulatory domains, where knowledge is expressed through obligations, permissions, prohibitions, conditions, and exceptions that require disciplined representation. Existing LLM-based extraction approaches improve scalability, but often struggle to maintain structural consistency in the generated ontology. We present a schema- and pattern-guided approach for regulatory ontology synthesis, in which LLM extraction is constrained directly within a target ontology rather than mapped to it afterward. The method incorporates human expertise through iterative prompt refinement, SHACL shape authoring, and repair-function design. It operates in two steps: structured decomposition of source text into typed components, followed by ontology generation guided by (i) a foundational schema that provides class and property whitelists, and (ii) ontology design patterns retrieved through embedding similarity to support structural alignment. A layered validation architecture combines SHACL conformance checking with SHACL-informed deterministic repair to address property-domain and type-discipline errors introduced during generation. We evaluate the approach through a multi-stage framework covering quality metrics, ontology correctness, and source-text faithfulness. The method is demonstrated on education funding regulations across four jurisdictions, showing that schema- and pattern-constrained generation supports the synthesis of structurally consistent regulatory ontologies.
